title: Debugging mystery: the pod that won't stay up
intro: 3 p.m. You just shipped a release and the api pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff. Production is degraded and the channel is getting loud. Work the problem: at each step, pick your next move.

start.situation:
$ kubectl get pods
NAME                READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
api-7d9f8c-abc12    0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   6          4m

The pod keeps starting and dying. What do you do first?

choices.label: kubectl delete pod api-7d9f8c-abc12  (just restart it)

delete.situation:
$ kubectl delete pod api-7d9f8c-abc12
pod "api-7d9f8c-abc12" deleted

The Deployment recreates it. 30 seconds later: CrashLoopBackOff again. You changed nothing and burned two minutes.
delete.text: Deleting a crashing pod just restarts the same broken thing. Diagnose before you act.

describe.situation:
$ kubectl describe pod api-7d9f8c-abc12
...
State:          Waiting
  Reason:       CrashLoopBackOff
Last State:     Terminated
  Reason:       Error
  Exit Code:    1
Events:
  Warning  BackOff   Back-off restarting failed container

Exit code 1: the container started, ran, then exited with an error. describe tells you THAT it failed, not WHY. Where next?

choices.label: Suspect the image tag is wrong

image.situation:
$ kubectl get deploy api -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
mycorp/api:1.4.2

The image pulled fine and the container actually started (it ran, then exited 1). An image/pull problem would show ImagePullBackOff or ErrImagePull, not a clean start-then-die.
image.text: Exit code 1 after the container starts is a RUNTIME failure, not an image problem. The application logs hold the answer.

logs.situation:
$ kubectl logs api-7d9f8c-abc12 --previous
Starting api v1.4.2...
Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND db-prod
    at Connection.connect (/app/db.js:14:11)

The app dies on startup trying to reach the host 'db-prod'. What's the cause?

choices.label: A NetworkPolicy is blocking the connection
The DB hostname doesn't resolve (wrong Service name?)

dbdown.situation:
$ kubectl get pods -n data | grep db
db-prod-0   1/1   Running   0   20d

The database is up and has been for 20 days. And the error was ENOTFOUND (name resolution), not 'connection refused' or a timeout.
dbdown.text: ENOTFOUND means DNS could not resolve the name at all. A down database would give 'connection refused' or a timeout, after the name resolved. Read the error precisely.

netpol.situation:
$ kubectl get networkpolicy
No resources found in this namespace.

There are no NetworkPolicies, so nothing is blocking traffic. And a blocked connection fails AFTER DNS resolves, with a timeout or refusal, not ENOTFOUND.
netpol.text: ENOTFOUND happens before any packet is sent, at the DNS step. NetworkPolicies affect connections that already resolved. The clue points at the name, not the path.

hostname.situation:
$ kubectl get svc
NAME   TYPE        CLUSTER-IP    PORT(S)
db     ClusterIP   10.96.12.7    5432/TCP

The Service that fronts the database is named 'db', but the app is trying to reach 'db-prod'. That name has no Service, so cluster DNS returns ENOTFOUND. How do you confirm where 'db-prod' comes from?

choices.label: Check the app's DB_HOST env value on the Deployment

fix.text: Solved! The release shipped a config that pointed at a hostname ('db-prod') no Service exposed, so DNS returned ENOTFOUND and the app crashed on startup, over and over. The method that got you here: read the exact error (ENOTFOUND = DNS), trust the logs over hunches, and verify config against what actually exists in the cluster.
